exact_statement: For a finite uniform exclusive independent-core controller, define U=sum_j q_j[H(u_j)-phi(m_j^2)] and R=sum_j phi(q_j)(1-m_j^2), phi(s)=s log2(1/s). At an actual physical controller query X write kappa=R-E R_child. If one Boolean X-child is a constant sign and all nonconstant selected cores occur only on the other child, 0<=D_X H(F)-kappa<=(3+2/ln2)Inf_X(F). If the two actual Boolean X-children use disjoint physical blocks, with distinct independent cores and disjoint private controllers on the two branches, 0<=D_X H(F)-kappa<=(4+2/ln2)Inf_X(F). These bounds retain biased and constant endpoints, and use the same physically reached selectors, cores and kappa, not independent replacements for a repeated core. For the two-core priority gate with one shared and one private control per event, either orientation, every finite adaptive tree respecting controller order X,A,B and stopped with its actual controller label resolved satisfies H(F_root)<=U_root+R_root+(3/ln2)T_data+(4+2/ln2)Pi_ctrl+E I(F_leaf)/ln2, where T_data=sum_data w q_j beta_j^2<=Pi_data and I(F_root)=Pi_data+Pi_ctrl+E I(F_leaf). Arbitrary fresh data exposure may be interleaved; inherited U_root remains explicit, and R_root and the residual costs are distinct influence debits. No arbitrary-core entropy or full FEI payment is claimed.

exact_statement: For two priority point tests on disjoint private controller blocks selecting independent disjoint Boolean cores u,v and default +1, at every actual later-test controller query before the earlier point test is settled, the original fine reserve R=sum eta(q_j)Var(u_j) satisfies 0<=D-kappa<=(6+2/ln2)Inf, kappa=R-E R_child, including arbitrary preceding data restrictions. More precisely, if a is the remaining earlier-event probability, q the remaining later-event probability, mu=Eu, nu=Ev, b=1-nu and d=(1-a)q b, then B-kappa=(q-2q^2)b^2(1-a)+a(1-a)Phi((mu-1+q b)^2,(q b)^2)+Phi((1-a(1-mu)-d)^2,d^2)<=(4-4q+4a)d<=6d when a<=1/2; a=1 is irrelevant and all charges vanish. Combining the accepted repeated-fallback earlier-test bound gives, for every finite adaptive physical tree with arbitrary private controller order and arbitrary data interleavings, H_root<=U_root+R_root+(3/ln2)T_data+(8+2/ln2)Pi_ctrl+E[H_leaf-U_leaf-R_leaf]. This also holds when both point events include one shared physical controller bit, in either orientation, provided that bit is queried first. At actual controller-resolved frontiers the last expectation is <=E I_leaf/ln2. The original fine selector reserve, actual physical repeated cores, inherited U and actual terminal functions are retained. No arbitrary-order multi-test, overlapping-data or universal FEI claim is made.
